analysis.title: "Melting Down": Goldman Admits Its Credit Bear Case Isn't Bearish Enough As AI Stress Hits Bonds
key_insights: Goldman's chief credit strategist Amanda Lynam says US spreads are quickly approaching the March 2026 peaks (93bp IG, 335bp HY) that Goldman had set as the base case in a downside scenario, and now expects spreads to moderately overshoot those ranges.

Lynam sees risks to Goldman's spread forecasts as firmly tilted toward more widening through early December, but says a material, sustained widening would require a sharp downturn in economic activity, which is not the base case.
Goldman's year-end spread targets are modestly tighter than current valuations. Goldman says this largely reflects typical late-December spread tightening as supply slows.

Tony Pasquariello (Goldman, head of hedge fund products) writes that corporate credit price action has been ugly and not limited to AI. Credit contacts described the market as 'melting down' more than once.
Pasquariello names POWER and CAPITAL as the two constraints on AI buildout as forward spending commitments stack up. He says the mega caps continue to execute well.
Goldman's AI basket was down 23% since June as of Thursday's close. Pasquariello's AI leaders basket has rolled over while S&P ex-AI is tracking for its best month in three years.

Goldman prime brokerage saw the largest wave of long selling in more than a year on Thursday. Hedge funds de-grossed in seven of the last eight sessions, and Information Technology saw its largest net selling since September 2024.
Goldman's HF VIP pair basket posted its worst week in 15 years (-4.1% over five sessions). The High Momentum basket has erased all YTD gains in a 43% drawdown.
Goldman's TMT AI vs. AI At-Risk basket fell 10% Thursday, its worst day since DeepSeek. It peaked at +94% YTD in June and is now down 13% for the year.
Goldman's IG Hyperscaler basket closed 17bps wider, its worst week on record outside of July. The HY Data Center basket (GSHYAIDC) fell 0.95pts in a 'somewhat orderly' move.
Goldman's 30-year Hyperscaler basket hit new wides and trades +85bps cheap to the IG100 ex-Hyperscaler basket, a 90bps move since launch in February.

Brad Shelofsky (head of IG credit trading) says the week was a significant re-rating of AI risk as markets reassessed the feasibility of funding the buildout, plus broad, aggressive de-grossing. He admits he fell into the mean reversion trap too early.

SpaceX: Musk said there is a small but non-zero possibility of over 20GW of compute online next year, and confidence in an incremental ~10GW. SpaceX had 1.7GW at end of Q3 and plans 3GW by year-end, at roughly $50B per GW. A previously reported $40B chip financing is now expected to likely price next week.
SpaceX SPCX 5.35% 2031s ended the week 55bps wider (T+225) and the 6.65% 2056s about 25bps wider (T+285).

Meta reported its first negative FCF quarter since its 2012 IPO. A 14C filing says timing is important to secure capital before competitors saturate funding options. Meta CDS hit a record after earnings.
Nvidia's Jensen Huang said demand for capital is much greater than the availability of capital, and that this will get solved.
ZeroHedge tallies total hyperscaler off-balance-sheet debt at $3.6 trillion as of Oct 21 (with META and SPCX reporting), and expects it to pass $4 trillion when the rest report.

Goldman's EMEA distressed desk: CCC spreads widened 55 to 65bps to 1,320-1,340bps. Global IG widened to 17-month wides of 129bps. Only 10.1% of the loan market trades above par, and primary markets remain largely closed.

The distressed desk reports the largest single-day hedge fund drawdown since Covid. CoreWeave 30mm traded as the structure continued to leak lower. Virgin Media bonds fell again with the desk 'out of explanations away from technicals'.

France: the 10-year OAT-Bund spread widened to 178bps, the widest since 2011, and French 10Y yields topped 5% for the first time since 2002. French bank subordinated debt widened about 25 to 30bps and Xover widened about 23.9bps on the week.
Goldman's EU macro credit desk says credit is underperforming rates for the first time in ages, and the usual sellers of junior protection did not show up.
Pasquariello still sees +18% S&P EPS growth in 2027 and notes bear markets with double-digit earnings growth are rare. He is cutting risk and has no issue 'swimming a bit closer to shore'.

Shelofsky still expects a July-style squeeze in Q4, but not until the Meta and SpaceX chip deals clear. Year-end de-grossing is a headwind. IG portfolio-trade inquiry had clients selling 1.3:1 by notional, and he sees $30-35bn of primary supply next week.
Upcoming catalysts: SpaceX chip financing pricing, Meta deal, GOOGL, AMZN and MSFT earnings, and an Oracle investor day on Wednesday.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's year-end spread targets are modestly tighter than today, reflecting typical late-December tightening as supply slows. Base case is that a sustained widening needs a sharp economic downturn. Shelofsky expects a July-style squeeze in Q4 once the Meta and SpaceX deals clear.
tension_points.bear_case: Goldman expects spreads to moderately overshoot the March 2026 peaks, with risks firmly tilted toward more widening into early December. Hyperscalers keep issuing, funds are de-grossing into year-end, and primary markets are largely closed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Meta and SpaceX chip deals pricing at wider concessions and further hyperscaler supply would invalidate the squeeze thesis. A sharp downturn in economic activity would turn the widening material and sustained.

tension_points.bull_case: Pasquariello sees +18% S&P EPS growth in 2027 and notes bear markets with double-digit earnings growth are rare. Positioning washes out, and S&P ex-AI is tracking for its best month in three years.
tension_points.bear_case: Goldman's AI basket is down 23% since June and credit contacts describe the market as 'melting down'. Funding costs for AI buildout are rising with power and capital as binding constraints.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Successful clearing of the Meta and SpaceX chip deals at tighter spreads would support the bull view. Continued widening in the 30-year hyperscaler basket beyond the new wides would support the bear view.
